llm.summary: The skill claims to be a marketing analysis tool but contains hard-coded API keys, runs arbitrary shell commands (including starting Xvfb / chrome), and tries to invoke a script from another skill in the user's home — several incoherences that warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (multi-platform content analysis, title/script generation) matches many files (analysis JSON, marketing_hub.js). However: (1) scripts/config.js contains prepopulated API keys even though manifest declares no required env vars and instructs the user to run a config command; (2) scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py references and will attempt to execute another skill's script under ~/.openclaw-agent2/... which is outside this skill's stated scope; (3) marketing_hub.js executes system utilities (curl, chrome, Xvfb) though the manifest declares only 'node' allowed — these capabilities are inconsistent with the minimalist installation instructions and declared requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only shows cloning and running node commands with two API tokens; it does not mention that runtime code may: spawn shell commands (curl), start/stop Xvfb, invoke /usr/bin/google-chrome, execute arbitrary exec/execSync calls, or call a run_render.py located in another skill under the user's home directory. The runtime instructions therefore understate the actions the code will take and grant broad discretion to execute system commands and other local skill scripts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No network download/extract install spec is present (instruction-only + included code files), so there is no direct remote installer risk. That said, the code will call external binaries (curl, chrome, Xvfb) at runtime; those binaries are not declared as required but are used. The lack of an explicit install step reduces remote-install risk but does not eliminate runtime execution risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest declares no required env vars or primary credential, but scripts/config.js in the bundle contains apparently live API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). This is a major inconsistency: secrets are committed in the repo despite manifest instructions to not commit config.js. The skill also constructs curl commands embedding the DEEPSEEK_KEY. The presence of committed keys and the ability to send HTTP requests with them is disproportionate and risky.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest sets always: false (good) and claims it does not modify other skills, but code attempts to locate and execute a script in ~/.openclaw-agent2/workspace-collector/skills/chanjing-one-click-video-creation/scripts/run_render.py — this implies cross-skill execution and dependence on user-local skill artifacts. The skill also creates files under an agent_data/chanjing_videos path and under its scripts/memory directory. The combination of executing other skills' scripts and running system-level commands (pkill, Xvfb, chrome) contradicts the declared limited privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill, consider the following: 

- Do not trust the hard-coded secrets: scripts/config.js contains API keys. Treat them as compromised: rotate any real keys that match these patterns and never use the included keys. The manifest even claimed config.js would not be committed, but it is present — this is a red flag.

- Runtime will execute shell commands (curl), start Xvfb, and try to run /usr/bin/google-chrome; these are not declared in required binaries. Running the skill can execute arbitrary system commands on your machine — avoid running it on production or sensitive hosts.

- The skill attempts to call a script in ~/.openclaw-agent2/... (another skill). That allows cross-skill execution and gives this skill potential access to other local skill code; inspect that path on your system before running. If you don't have that other skill, the script will return an error, but if present it will run with your account privileges.

- The manifest declared subprocess allowedPatterns only for node, but the code uses exec/execSync to invoke many other commands; this is an internal mismatch and suggests sloppy or unsafe engineering.

- If you still want to use it: (1) audit marketing_hub.js and cmd_vid_integration.py fully; (2) remove or replace the included scripts/config.js and run node marketing_hub.js config with your own keys stored securely (do not commit); (3) run in an isolated environment (container or disposable VM) and without exposing real credentials; (4) monitor outbound network to the declared hosts (api.tikhub.io, api.deepseek.com) and any other endpoints; (5) prefer obtaining this tool from the upstream repository and verify its integrity; (6) rotate API keys if you ever used the embedded ones.
